name: Gold Star Timer
tagline: The app's own gold star sticker, slapped over the rim of its rainbow countdown: the timer and the reward in one mark.
concept: This is Classroom Widgets' real timer: a cream face and the widget's own horizontal rainbow gradient (red at 9, green at 12 and 6, violet at 3) with its round caps, drained by a quarter so only the thin pale track remains from 9 to 12, which is how the widget actually depletes. On top sits the app's Font Awesome star sticker (orange-500 with a lighter centre, thick white die-cut border, down-right shadow, tilted +15° in the app's 5° steps), slapped big over the rim at 4:40 as a co-hero rather than a badge, and ring, rim and star all sit inside the 80% maskable circle. It is exactly what a class sees on the board, the countdown plus the gold star at time's up. The amber plate is the app's canvas, with a thin cream edge so it separates when shown on that canvas, and the face is left empty; the dark variant uses the app's dark-mode timer (warm-grey face, toned rainbow) and keeps a toned warm-white border so the orange star never sinks into the deep caramel plate. With no numeral, identity comes from the ring itself: its outer edge is a clean closed circle, the spent quarter is a thinner track rather than a gap, and its only opening is where the star physically covers it, bounded by star-shaped occlusion edges, so it cannot read as a C, a spinner or a refresh arrow. The glyph is the icon with colour removed: the same geometry refit to the box at SF Symbols weight, with the star's white die-cut border becoming a 104-unit knockout; in the live menu-bar state the thick band retreats from its 9 o'clock cap back toward 12 over the track as a timer runs, the star stays stuck at 4:40, and at zero only the track and the star remain while the star gives one bounce.
glyphNotes: At 18px it reads as a closed timer ring (2.2px band, with a 1.5px thinner quarter at upper left for the spent time) broken only at lower right by a chunky 7.6px five-point star across a 1.8px die-cut gap. That makes it a sticker on a ring rather than a C, G, magnifier or refresh arrow, since there is no arrowhead and no round-capped opening. The silhouette is one solid ring piece plus one solid Font Awesome star in #000 only; the smallest features are the 66-unit star tips, the 84-unit track and the 104-unit moat.

name: Mini Board
tagline: The projected board in one glance: the rainbow timer out front, the name-picker card tucked behind it, and an orange star sticker pinning the two together.
concept: A thumbnail of the board teachers actually project. It keeps the client's round-2 charm but is rebuilt to hold at every size. The hero is the app's cream timer face (left empty) in its round-capped rainbow ring. Tucked behind it is the randomiser card with its real purple→pink→amber reel: faded names peek in at top and bottom, and the chosen name sits bold on a white chip. The app's own Font Awesome star sticker, in orange with a thick white die-cut border, pins the card's corner where it meets the timer's rim, and a few flecks of the red/yellow/teal/navy confetti finish the scene. Everything sits inside the 80% maskable circle on the amber canvas plate, which has two large facets and a cream keyline so it separates on the app's own canvas. With no numeral, the ring gets its identity from its spent sixth and from what surrounds it. From 10 to 12 o'clock the rainbow steps down onto a thin track, so every rendering is a closed, notched O with round caps, never a C, spinner or refresh arrow, while the card behind it and the star in its crook make it the board. The star sits outside the ring, never in a gap, so nothing reads as a crescent-and-star, cloud or sync badge. Each size gets its own rendering: the full scene from 64 px up; a macOS dark variant re-lit with a walnut plate, warm-grey card frame, the app's dark timer face with a dark spent channel, toned rims and no glare; a flat small master for 16–32 px that keeps only card, ring and star, bigger, with two white name bars, a smooth sweep, white die-cut borders, no confetti or facets, snapped to the grid; and a one-tone glyph that is the same drawing with colour removed, where the white rims become 64-unit knockouts. Live menu-bar state: while a timer runs, the glyph's thick band retreats counter-clockwise onto the thin track in step with the in-app ring, and at zero only the track, the card and the star remain.
glyphNotes: At 18 pt it reads as an outlined name card (a frame plus two name bars) with a bold, closed timer ring overlapping its lower-right and a solid star pinning its lower-left corner. It is one #000 path drawn on the 16 px grid (1 px frame and name bars, 2 px ring, 5–6 px star, 1 px knockouts), so it stays crisp at true 1x in the Windows tray and GNOME bar and sits at SF Symbols weight beside Wi-Fi and Control Centre; the ring is the heaviest stroke, and its 60° spent notch, the same notch the colour icon draws as its pale track, shows from 18 pt @2x up.
